The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=0,$ the particle is located at the position $x=-2.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=4?$

The position of the particle at $t=4$ is $x=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=4$ is equal to its position at $t=0$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [0,4].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(4)=x(0)+{\int }_{0}^{4}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(0)=-2$, and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{0}^{4}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=0$ to $t=4.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}v(t)\,\text{d}t=12.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(4)=-2+12=10.
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=4$ is $x=10.$
